summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her fifth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. The chemotherapy was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m² to minimize toxicity, and she did not develop mucositis. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately, becoming undetectable on two consecutive days. She developed marked pancytopenia requiring neutropenic precautions but remained afebrile without need for antibiotics. Her diabetes was managed with an insulin sliding scale during the admission, and metformin was resumed at discharge. Oral vancomycin was continued for prior C. difficile infection. IVIG was administered on day three, and she received prophylactic pentamidine. Wound care was optimized for a stage II pressure ulcer on the coccyx and elbow skin changes. She was discharged home with close oncology follow-up.
